problem:
Which of the following augmented matrices are in row echelon form?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 0 & 8 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}],\,\,B=[\begin{aligned}8 & 7 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}],\,\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 & 7 \\ 3 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying Augmented Matrices in Row Echelon Form
examples.problem:
Which of the following augmented matrices are in row echelon form?

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}
$$
examples.worked_solution:
Remember that an augmented matrix is in row echelon form if its coefficient matrix satisfies the following conditions:

- All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.

- Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The first matrix is not in row echelon form since $a_{32} \neq 0$ (condition II is violated).

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}
$$

- The second matrix is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}
$$

- The third matrix is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}
$$

- The fourth matrix is not in row echelon form since, for example, the leading entry $a_{22}$ lies to the left of the leading entry $a_{13}$ (condition II is violated).

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following matrices are in row echelon form?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 6 & 10 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Remember that a matrix is in row echelon form if it satisfies the following conditions:

- All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.
- Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$  is not in row echelon form since ${a}_{32}\ne 0$ (condition II is violated). 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 6 & 10 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $C$ is not in row echelon form since the second row contains only zeros and it is not at the bottom of the matrix (condition I is violated).

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, only $B$ is in row echelon form.
